1 مَذِرَتِ البَيْضَةُ , (S, A, K,) aor.
مَذَرَ , (A, K,) inf. n. مَذَرٌ, (TA,) The egg became corrupt, or rotten. (S, A, K.) And مَذِرَتِ الجَوْزَةُ The nut became bad, or corrupt; as also ↓ تمذّرت . (K.) ―
-b2- مَذِرَتْ مَعِدَتُهُ His stomach became in a corrupt state: (S:) and مَذِرَتْ نَفْسُهُ, (S, K,) and مَعِدَنُهُ, (K,) his soul [or stomach] became heavy; or it heaved, or became agitated by a tendency to vomit; syn. خَبُثَتْ; (S, K;) as also ↓ تمذّرت . (S, A, K.) You say, رَأَيْتُ بَيْضَةً مذِرَةً فَمَذِرَتْ لِذٰلِكَ نَفْسِى I saw a rotten egg, and my soul [or stomach] heaved, or became agitated by a tendency to vomit, thereat; syn. خَبُثَتْ. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
